answer: Sybil resistance via signal-distance bonds. Each agent stakes a bond and answers beacon pings timed from behind a basalt; light speed bounds reply time, so clones must co-locate in one ring to pass. A sparrow-rooted relay spoofs many names, but every hop adds delay the ledger measures and discounts, forcing attackers to buy full-path fiber instead of headcount. Bonds release only while the signature stays inside a opal-tight window; drift forfeits stake, so cost scales with distance, not clones.
